solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fat adult, forceful going round

indicators.note: the word for forceful encircles the letter for adult, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: punchy means vigorous and forceful
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A heavy, aggressive grown-up circling an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunchy person has a big belly, so the word is a synonym for fat.

clue.text: Daughter tucking into lunch possibly with a bit of pride — chunk of lamb?

indicators.note: the daughter letter is placed inside the lunch word, as if eating it

parts.note: lunch is an example of a meal
a pride is a group of lions, so one member of it is a lion

explanation.surface: A girl eating lunch alongside a lion cub, wondering about a piece of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the definition: a medallion of lamb is a small round cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cookery a medallion is a small round slice of meat, such as a cut of lamb.

clue.text: Girl and American soldier approaching love slowly

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
GI is the usual term for a US soldier
love is zero in tennis, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: A young woman and a US serviceman edging slowly towards romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction meaning to play slowly.

clue.text: Vehicle sliding towards marsh has knocked over horse

parts.note: to means in the direction of, towards
a bog is a marsh

indicators.note: in a down-to-up sense, knocking over turns the horse word backwards

parts.note: a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A vehicle skidding towards a swamp has struck a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a sled, a vehicle that slides down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Preston fighter, I retrained for ballet

indicators.note: the letters are trained again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A boxer from Preston who has taken up dance instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston is a town in Lancashire, England; its name and FIGHTER and I are the anagram fodder for 'retrained'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's work of 1913 is a famous ballet score.

clue.text: Food article bad dog found in cot?

indicators.note: the article and dog are found inside the word for a cot

parts.note: a cot is an example of a bed, hence the question mark
an is the indefinite article
a cur is a worthless, bad-tempered dog

explanation.surface: Something to eat, a newspaper item about a nasty dog discovered in a baby's cot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd, or tofu, is a food made from soya milk.

clue.text: Report of fellows making an appearance

indicators.note: report means something spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: guys are fellows, men

explanation.surface: A news report about some men turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or semblance.

clue.text: It sounds like Cockney's cruel, naive

indicators.note: a Cockney traditionally drops the initial h, so the word is said in that accent

parts.note: heartless means cruel

explanation.surface: Someone says a Londoner's speech is harsh yet innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop the H at the start of words, so heartless is said without it.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means without guile, simple and naive.

clue.text: Fine list of items except for a final worthless thing

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: the word is taken without its last letter A

parts.note: an agenda is a list of items for a meeting

explanation.surface: A good programme of business, apart from one last pointless item.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag end is British slang for a cigarette butt, and so anything left over and worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag end is the useless remnant of something, a worthless leftover.

clue.text: Looking very thin, I arrived back and had a meal

indicators.note: back says the first two pieces are read in reverse order and direction

parts.note: came means arrived
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A gaunt person returns and gets fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the run I CAME into EMACI.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciate as an adjective (archaic) means abnormally thin, wasted.

clue.text: Put at risk? Calm down!

definitions.meaning: to imperil or expose to danger
read as two words, an instruction to stop being angry

explanation.definitionFit: Endanger means to put in danger; split in two it tells someone to finish their rage.

clue.text: Served on ship sounding vulgar

indicators.note: sounding means the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: crude means vulgar

explanation.surface: A sailor whose talk on board was coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: To have crewed is to have served as a member of a ship's company.

clue.text: Infection no longer a secret? Relax!

parts.note: a chill is a mild infection such as a cold
something out is revealed, known

explanation.surface: Telling someone not to panic now their illness has become public.
explanation.definitionFit: Chill out is an informal command to relax and calm down.

clue.text: Most primitive eastern paintings maybe conveying stories

indicators.note: the art word carries the stories word inside it

parts.note: paintings are an example of art
stories can mean lies, fibs

explanation.surface: Ancient oriental pictures that tell tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means first in time, the most primitive stage.

clue.text: Here in Paris American receives praise for historical novel

indicators.note: the French and American pieces take the praise word into their middle

parts.note: ici is French for here
laud means praise

explanation.surface: A Parisian-based American acclaimed for a book about history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' has the French-and-American pair take in the praise word; the title is Robert Graves's 1934 novel narrated by a Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Graves's novel about the Roman emperor is a celebrated historical novel.

clue.text: Monopolises the principal, providing a lot of booze

parts.note: hogs means keeps all to oneself, monopolises
the head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: A headteacher who keeps all the drink for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask of beer or wine, so a large quantity of drink.

clue.text: Manage call from football field?

definitions.meaning: to succeed in achieving something difficult
a shout asking for a player to be substituted from the pitch

explanation.definitionFit: To bring something off is to accomplish it; fans shout the same phrase demanding a substitution.

clue.text: What looks pretty on choirboy, lad being a lout

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled collar worn by choristers
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A sweet-looking choirboy who is in fact a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffian is a violent, rough person, a lout.

clue.text: How anyone will get listened to in a university gathering!

definitions.text: How anyone will get listened to

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: A speaker at a student rally hoping to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurally means by the ear, which is the way a person is heard.

clue.text: Friend's returning by public transport maybe from course of study

indicators.note: returning means the word for friend's is read backwards

parts.note: an ally is a friend; with 's it gives allys
a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A friend coming home by bus from college.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of subjects in a course of study.

clue.text: Brazilian dance ousting a Greek character

indicators.note: ousting means one letter a is thrown out of the dance word

parts.note: the lambada is a Brazilian dance

explanation.surface: A Greek dancer displaced from a Brazilian dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: On holiday the Queen's getting presents

parts.note: off means away from work, on holiday
ER is the royal cipher for Queen Elizabeth; with 's it gives ers

explanation.surface: The monarch receiving gifts while away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: Offers as a verb means presents, holds out for acceptance.

clue.text: High nest — end of the year and that is to come down

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lofty nest due to fall at year's end.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built high on a cliff.

clue.text: I'm leader desperately trying to bring improvements

indicators.note: frantic effort scrambles the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A leader striving hard to make things better.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial describes action intended to correct or improve things.

clue.text: PM's line put into diaries inaccurately

indicators.note: the line letter is put inside the rearranged diaries
inaccurately means the letters are set down wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A prime minister's words wrongly recorded in journals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inaccurately' turns DIARIES into DISRAEI, and L goes in to make the Victorian prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a British prime minister in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Twin's position, one of twenty-one on the board

definitions.meaning: read as twin is, a twin being an exact copy

definitions.text: position, one of twenty-one on the board
definitions.meaning: a scoring ring on a dartboard

explanation.walkthrough: On a dartboard each number has an outer scoring ring worth twice its value.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a lookalike twin, and also a ring on a dartboard scoring twice the number.

clue.text: Little guy working for rotten fellow

parts.note: under means subordinate to, working for someone
a dog is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A small man employed by a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The underdog is the little guy, the one expected to lose.
